# Planned scope

**Status:** planning outline. This project does not contain a completed Volume III
manuscript. The volume builds on the core methods of Volume I and the adjusted
and specialist methods of Volume II.

The purpose is to assess scientific validity, extend models where the observation
structure requires it, validate prediction, synthesise evidence, and reproduce
the analytical record. Complexity should follow the question and design.

| Planned chapter | Intended contribution |
|:----------------|:----------------------|
| 1. Causal thinking | Causal diagrams, confounding, mediation, selection, and identification assumptions |
| 2. Regression extensions | Interaction, non-linear relationships, stratification, and model comparison |
| 3. Model-building strategy | Prespecification, complexity, overfitting, variable selection, and sensitivity analyses |
| 4. Longitudinal data | Within-person dependence, time structure, and fixed and random effects |
| 5. Mixed models | Supported implementations, time-by-group effects, and model assumptions |
| 6. Survival extensions | Time-varying predictors, non-proportional hazards, and competing-risk distinctions |
| 7. Risk prediction | Calibration, discrimination, internal and external validation, and clinical use |
| 8. Diagnostic comparisons | ROC comparisons, threshold evaluation, and clinical utility |
| 9. Method comparison | Bland–Altman differences, limits of agreement, measurement bias, and assumptions |
| 10. Meta-analysis | Effect scales, study weights, fixed and random effects, and heterogeneity |
| 11. Small-study and reporting effects | Funnel plots, appropriate tests, selective reporting, and interpretation limits |
| 12. jamovi and R integration | Rj, generated syntax, reproducible scripts, packages, and dependency records |
| 13. Reproducible research | Data and analysis documentation, versioning, reporting standards, and review records |
| 14. Clinical prediction case | Development, validation, calibration, decision context, and transparent reporting |
| 15. Public health survey case | Design variables, weights, clustering, and supported complex-survey analysis |

## Delivery requirements

Use the common clinical sequence and a separate Hands-on section. Distinguish
conceptual orientation from an implemented, tested workflow. Advanced analyses
may need jamovi modules or R packages; document the dependency, version, method,
and support limits for each worked case. Availability must be verified when the
chapter is written rather than assumed from this outline.

Correlation and regression are introduced in Volume I; adjusted modeling and
basic model assessment are developed in Volume II. This volume adds explicit
causal assumptions, longitudinal extensions, prediction validation, evidence
synthesis, and a fuller computational record. Advanced claims need methods that
match the design and target quantity.

The prediction case should include a stated intended use, adequate development
data, honest performance assessment, calibration, and validation. The survey case
should preserve design information rather than treating weighted, clustered
observations as a simple independent sample. Meta-analysis should distinguish
heterogeneity from bias and uncertainty in individual studies.

Planned appendices include advanced assumption checklists, reporting checklists,
a model-development template, and extended datasets. These remain future work.
